transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 16:00 PT | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Olivia (BluePeak HoMLOps), Daniel (CTO), Sanjay (Lead DE)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intro then dive into cost and perf, uh Ethan will cover the technical levers.
00:18 Olivia: thanks Maya, quick note we pulled this meeting together to understand your cost per inference and what moves we have to meet our monthly budget, which is around $15k for this phase.
00:30 Maya: perfect, yep that's what we're here for. quick round of intros?
00:36 Daniel: Daniel Park, CTO, we run high-volume signal gen, mostly short sequences but some long-context backtests.
00:44 Sanjay: Sanjay, build infra and pipelines, curious about batching and cache mechanics, and also private deployment options.
00:50 Ethan: cool, so to start at high level Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For cost econ we look at three levers: per-token pricing, batching (higher tokens/sec amortization), and caching/prefix KV cache.
01:10 Olivia: can you translate that into expected $/query? our requests are typically 60 tokens output, 40 tokens prompt avg.
01:20 Ethan: sure ballpark — on hosted using model x-small-open (example) you'd see roughly $0.0006 per token for generation on that class, so 100 tokens => $0.06 per call. But with batching and persistent KV cache that can drop 30-60% depending on request similarity and hit rate.
01:42 Daniel: wait that per-token seems high compared to our current vendor, we pay about $0.04 per call for similar outputs. what's the delta?
01:50 Maya: good Q. Two points: first vendor's baseline model and latency differ, and second our pricing includes optimized kernels and throughput SLAs for production; in bulk/predictable workloads Dedicated can be much cheaper because you reserve GPU and get better unit cost.
02:10 Ethan: right, for Dedicated we run capacity sizing; e.g., a c5-type pool (example) at steady state might lower per-token to $0.0002-$0.00035 range depending on utilization and batching efficiency. So same 100-token call could be $0.02-$0.035.
02:30 Sanjay: what's the utilization assumptions? if we underutilize we pay for reserved capacity right?
02:36 Ethan: exactly — committed utilization matters. We model two scenarios: conservative (60% util) and optimized (80-90% via batching and auto-burst). We also offer burst to hosted pool to smooth peaks.
02:52 Olivia: can you explain caching in plain terms? we have a lot of repeated prefixes for backtest prompts.
02:58 Ethan: sure, prefix/KV cache stores previously computed key-value pairs for transformer layers for identical prefixes — so you don't re-compute tokens for common warmup prompts. If 40% of your calls share prefixes you can see big savings since you only compute deltas. Caching is enabled on both Hosted and Dedicated; Private you manage network but we support same cache logic.
03:20 Daniel: does caching require special model changes or is it transparent?
03:24 Ethan: mostly transparent at runtime; you do need to ensure deterministic tokenization and stable model checkpoints. we sometimes recommend quantized variants which are cache-friendly.
03:36 Olivia: quantization — how does that affect quality? we're doing trading signals so mistakes are sensitive.
03:42 Ethan: quantization can reduce perf slightly but modern 4-bit/8-bit approaches keep NLL and answer quality close for many workloads. we recommend running a small eval set. that's part of the pilot.
03:58 Maya: question on security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, and audit logs. Do you have those?
04:06 Maya (slightly wrong): we mean, do you have SOC two...
04:08 Daniel: yeah we've heard mixed from other vendors.
04:10 Ethan: yes, Redwood has SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integrations, and per-request audit logs in the console. For Private we can also support on-prem with customer KMS and full network isolation.
04:26 Sanjay: any difference in logging retention across Hosted vs Private?
04:30 Maya: hosted has tiered retention, enterprise add-on gives longer retention; Private you control retention.
04:36 Olivia: ok good.
04:40 05:00 speaker1: (background) mm-hmm
05:12 Ethan: circling back to pricing math quickly — we'll run a model that takes your qps, avg seq length, and hit rate to estimate monthly spend. We ask for three sample distributions: low, median, peak.
05:30 Olivia: we can provide logs for last month, but anonymized.
05:36 Sanjay: note, latency targets: 90th percentile needs to be < 150ms for short queries or else our algo times out. Is that achievable on hosted?
05:46 Ethan: depends on model. Hosted with smaller optimized models typically hits that; for larger context or stricter p90 you may need Dedicated with pinned GPUs in region. We also do model routing — keep low-latency models on hot path.
06:10 Daniel: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated? if pilot works we might want to move in a month.
06:16 Maya: Dedicated procurement and setup is a few weeks — sizing and contract first, then deployment and canary. Private will take longer, usually 6-10 weeks for VPC/on-prem.
06:30 Sanjay: how do you handle model rollouts and A/B testing?
06:34 Ethan: Console supports rollouts, canary percentages, automatic fallback to previous model if regression detected, and we tie quality alerts to prompt sets.
06:46 Olivia: any concerns about cost predictability with batching? we worry about spikes causing high token counts and rumors of hidden costs.
06:54 Maya: two things — batching reduces unit cost but increases average latency a bit; we expose metrics in the console so you can see per-token breakdown and cost by route. Also for Dedicated you get committed spend which caps your unit economics variability.
07:12 Ethan: we also support QoS policies to prioritize latency-sensitive requests and batch background requests. That way you don't batch critical paths.
07:24 Daniel: curious about what a pilot looks like.
07:28 Maya: typical pilot — 1 week on Hosted with your sample traffic or replay, run a benchmark for throughput and latency, collect cost per token and hit rate. After that we propose Dedicated sizing if the numbers justify commit.
07:40 Olivia: what's the minimum pilot data we need?
07:44 Ethan: ideally one week of representative traffic or a few hours of high-volume replay. If you can't share live traffic, a synthetic replay with your seq length distribution is sufficient.
07:56 Sanjay: about pricing tiers — is model choice locked? e.g., if we start on small model and need to upgrade to a higher-capacity model mid-pilot, how's pricing handled?
08:04 Maya: we bill model usage; you can switch models and we provide delta estimates. For Dedicated you can pin versions but we support roll-forward. We'll show both marginal cost and committed amortized numbers.
08:18 Daniel: do you have examples of customers who moved from hosted to dedicated and what their cost drop was?
08:24 Maya: yes — a quant firm we worked with dropped per-token by ~55% after moving to Dedicated and tuning batching/caching; we can share an anonymized case study.
08:36 Olivia: can you also show how cache hit rate correlates to cost?
08:40 Ethan: absolutely — we'll include a chart in the spreadsheet mapping hit rates (0-80%) to % cost reduction.
08:48 Sanjay: technical deep dive: what happens if KV cache misses and we need long context recompute — is there an autoscale fallback?
08:56 Ethan: yes, autoscale and burst pools plus routing to compatible smaller variants. Also we have fallback to lower-cost regions if latency tolerances allow.
09:10 Olivia: any network egress considerations for private data?
09:14 Ethan: for Hosted traffic crosses our network; Private keeps traffic in your VPC and you control egress. We can support on-prem isolated deployments for the most sensitive workloads.
09:26 Daniel: let's talk numbers — Maya can you walk through an example scenario for our 15k/mo budget?
09:32 Maya: sure — if we assume 100k calls/month at 100 tokens average that's 10M tokens. On Hosted at $0.0006/token that's $6k/month; but that's illustrative — your model choice could raise it. With moderate caching and batching we project $3.2k. If you need lower cost for scale at Dedicated for 10M tokens we can get down to ~$1.8k depending on utilization.
09:56 Olivia: I'm surprised hosted is that cheap vs earlier numbers — is that because of different model assumptions?
10:02 Ethan: yes model family assumptions. We'll run the spreadsheet with your exact model and token counts.
10:10 Sanjay: for Dedicated what are minimum commits?
10:14 Maya: depends on region and GPU type — typically monthly reserved pools start at the low tens of thousands committed, but we have flexible entry levels for startups and growth customers. We'll propose a few tiers.
10:28 Daniel: ok.
10:30 10:35 speaker2: um huh
10:40 Ethan: quick note on observability — console shows token-level cost, route breakdowns, p50/p90 latencies, and per-prompt quality regression alerts.
10:54 Olivia: great.
11:00 Maya: ok I want to capture action items and next steps — Ethan will send recommended batching and cache config, I'll send the cost model and case study, and Olivia will send sample traffic.
11:12 Olivia: yes we'll share anonymized logs and a list of sensitive entites to scrub.
11:18 Daniel: timeline — can we aim to start pilot next week?
11:22 Maya: we can start pilot asap pending logs and NDAs; we'll follow up with a proposal by 2026-03-07 and a kickoff the week of 2026-03-09.
11:34 Sanjay: small nit — do you support VPC peering for Private?
11:38 Ethan: yes, VPC peering and dedicated interconnects available.
11:44 Olivia: anything else?
11:46 Maya: one more question — any compliance pre-reqs for pilot?
11:50 Ethan: basic NDA and access creds; for production we'll need SOC2 review and network diagram.
12:00 Olivia: ok thanks everyone.
12:04 Maya: thanks, we'll send docs and follow up.\nEnd summary recap (auto): Agreed next steps include sending cost model spreadsheet, running 1-week Hosted pilot, sharing SOC2 and network docs, and scheduling follow-up to evaluate Dedicated sizing.
